At the edge of the market, past a pile of wine barrels, I saw a big pair of shoulders.

Hunched back, magnificent beard, an old seal on his chest. No mistaking it. I gripped the cart handles and stopped breathing for three whole seconds.

"Closing up already, Riko Trading?" the dried-fish seller next door asked.

"No. Just, uh, inventory."

I pulled the cart behind the barrels and let the canvas down. Took off the showy shawl, too, the one I wear for business. With no patter on my face, I peeked through a gap between barrels at the street.

The back didn't turn toward me. It picked up an old pot from a stall, flipped it over, and stared hard at the bottom. That look hasn't changed at all.

All I had to do was call out. One sentence. "Long time no see." A sentence you couldn't put a price on.

"Um, miss?" the fish seller called over the barrels. "If you're hiding, you might want to take the sign down first."

I looked up. The "WONDERS" on my sign was sticking way out over the top of the barrels.

The shoulders started to turn, slowly. I hurriedly knocked the sign flat.

Hiding fee, behind the barrels: zero coppers. The night that followed was what ran up the bill.
